results.title: Recall lookup and product-level relevance
results.summary: Recall records are retrievable for the supported drugs, but product-level relevance cannot rely on structured fields: 15176 of 18110 drug enforcement records (83.8%) lack the openfda block. In the per-drug sample, 40.2% had openfda data, 87.0% had an NDC parsable from product_description, and 84 were combination products matched by a single-ingredient keyword.

results.title: Lot-specific matching where source data permits
results.summary: Lot information exists only as free text in code_info; 77.1% of sampled records contain an explicit lot token. Lot matching is possible only as a user-confirmed comparison, never as an automatic non-match.

results.title: Rate-limit and service-error handling
results.summary: 9 error scenarios exercised; 0 misclassified. HAZARD: openFDA answers a query on a nonexistent field with NOT_FOUND, so field-name bugs look like "no recalls". The app must run a known-positive control query per source (see TEST_PLAN RG-2). openFDA returns HTTP 500 (not 400) for malformed queries.

details.case: openFDA query on a nonexistent field (e.g., a typo in a field name)
details.expected: Hazard probe: if this is NO_MATCH, a field-name bug is indistinguishable from "no recalls"

results.title: Source freshness and retrieval timestamps
results.summary: Each source exposes a dataset-level freshness marker (openFDA meta.last_updated, DailyMed metadata.db_published_date, RxNav version). None exposes per-record last-modified for recalls; the app must store both the source marker and its own retrieval time.

results.title: Missing or ambiguous manufacturer / facility information
results.summary: 20 SPL documents parsed: 15 list no MANUFACTURE establishment (2 have no establishment section at all), 1 list more than one MANUFACTURE establishment, 13 contain REPACK/RELABEL operations. Observed MANUFACTURE code is C43360 (Document A states C43215). 15/15 repackager source-NDC traversals resolved to an originating labeler via openFDA. Facility identity is frequently absent or multi-valued and must be shown as uncertain, never as verified.

results.title: Sufficiency of direct API calls without an application backend
results.summary: Direct, keyless HTTPS calls are sufficient for identification (NDC Directory, RxNav), labeling/establishment data (DailyMed SPL) and recall retrieval (openFDA enforcement) in MVP scope. Limitations that a phone-only design must absorb: free-text recall matching on device; per-IP keyless quotas (a phone-only app sends no shared key); no FDA inspection/483/import-alert data via these four APIs; and SPL XML parsing on device.

notTested: FDA inspection classifications, Form 483s, warning letters and Import Alert 66-40 (Document A §2–3): not part of the four mandated APIs; deferred, see docs/API_FEASIBILITY.md.
HTTP 429 behavior under real quota exhaustion (not provoked to avoid exhausting the shared per-IP quota).
